props.title: Aether Student Resiliency Framework
props.description: A research-informed framework for clearer student-support conversations, learning habits, and intervention pathways with appropriate adult and institutional guidance.
props.keywords: student resiliency framework, student support, learning habits, evidence-led education, Aether framework

props.heading: Every student deserves a clearer path to support.
props.subheading: Aether Student Resiliency Framework • Live website
props.description: Aether is a live, research-informed starting point for turning “something feels hard” into a clearer, human-supported next step. Explore the experience first; then examine the public framework, its evidence, and its boundaries. It is not a clinical tool, diagnostic system, or validated intervention study.

props.heading: A simple path from uncertainty to a supported next step.
props.description: Aether gives a difficult-to-name situation a responsible shape: start with context, make learning patterns visible, and identify the person or pathway that can help next—without reducing a student to a score or diagnosis.

features.title: 01 · Notice the context
features.description: Start with the conditions around learning: how a student is able to participate, what feels difficult, and what they may need in order to ask for help.

features.title: 02 · Make patterns visible
features.description: Name practical routines, friction points, and supports so a conversation can move from a vague concern toward a specific, usable observation.

features.title: 03 · Involve the right support
features.description: Clarify who can help next and when qualified adult, school, safeguarding, or professional guidance needs to lead the conversation.

props.heading: A hopeful idea earns trust by showing its work.
props.description: The live experience comes first. The public record then makes the question, proposed method, and current limits visible before anyone decides whether a conversation or pilot is worthwhile.

items.title: Aether: a live starting point, not a final answer
items.description: Experience Aether first. Then use the documented model to assess the proposed student-support approach with mentors, educators, and potential collaborators.
items.question: How can a framework make wellbeing, learning habits, and intervention pathways easier to discuss and improve?
items.method: Define needs, map support touchpoints, identify meaningful signals, and turn the work into a usable, reviewable artifact.
items.evidence: Framework PDF, public portfolio documentation, and an open support-center workflow.
items.outcome: A shared starting point for feedback, adult-guided review, and ethical pilot-scoping discussions.
items.limitation: This is not a validated clinical, therapeutic, or school-wide intervention study. It should not replace qualified professional support.
items.nextStep: Gather structured reviewer feedback and define an ethical, measurable pilot scope with an appropriate supervising adult or institution.

props.heading: Before you begin
props.description: A few clear answers about what Aether is, what it is not, and how to use it responsibly.

faqs.question: What is the best way to begin?
faqs.answer: Start with the live experience. If you are considering Aether for a student, school, or program, then read the public framework with a mentor, educator, or other appropriate adult who can help place it in context.

faqs.question: Is Aether a clinical or diagnostic tool?
faqs.answer: No. It does not diagnose, treat, or replace qualified medical, mental-health, school, or safeguarding professionals.

faqs.question: What if someone needs immediate help?
faqs.answer: Aether is not an emergency or crisis service. Contact local emergency services or a qualified school, safeguarding, or mental-health professional. In the United States, call or text 988 for the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

faqs.question: Can a school adopt it as an intervention?
faqs.answer: Not on the basis of this public artifact alone. Any real-world pilot should have appropriate adult supervision, institutional review, safeguarding, and measurable evaluation.

props.heading: Start with the experience. Continue with care.
props.description: Visit the live Aether website to see the journey. If you are evaluating it for students or a school, review the public framework and bring the right people into the conversation before any real-world use.
